question: What minimum vertical clearance is required for overhead signs over the pavement and shoulders?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Overhead signs must provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, unless nearby structures have a lesser vertical clearance. This same 17-foot clearance applies to median-barrier post-mounted signs that overhang the traveled way, and to preferential lane signs mounted higher on median barriers where lateral clearance is limited. Standards (mandatory): - "Overhead signs shall provide a vertical clearance of not less than 17 feet to the sign, light fixture, or sign bridge over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, except where the structure on which the overhead signs are to be mounted or other structures along the roadway near the sign structure have a lesser vertical clearance." (Section 2A.15, shown in [Image 5]) - "Signs that are post-mounted on a median barrier that overhang any portion of the traveled way shall be mounted with a vertical clearance that complies with that of overhead signs." (Section 2A.15, shown in [Image 5]) - Related support-placement requirement: "For overhead sign supports, the minimum lateral offset from the edge of the shoulder (or if no shoulder exists, from the edge of the pavement) to the near edge of overhead sign supports (cantilever or sign bridges) shall be 6 feet. Overhead sign supports shall have a barrier or crash cushion to shield them if they are within the clear zone." Options (permitted): - If the vertical clearance of other structures along the roadway near the sign structure is less than 16 feet, the vertical clearance to an overhead sign structure or support may be as low as 1 foot higher than the vertical clearance of the other structures in order to improve visibility of the overhead signs (shown in [Image 5]). - In special cases the clearance to overhead signs may be reduced if necessary because of substandard dimensions in tunnels and other major structures such as double-deck bridges (shown in [Image 5]). - Where lateral clearance is limited, Preferential Lane regulatory signs post-mounted on a median barrier that are 72 inches or less in width may be mounted higher, such that the vertical clearance to the bottom of the sign, light fixture, or structural support, whichever is lowest, is not less than 17 feet above any portion of the pavement and shoulders. - The same 17-foot minimum applies where warning signs on median barriers for preferential lanes are mounted higher due to limited lateral clearance. - The same 17-foot minimum applies where Preferential Lane guide signs 72 inches or less in width are mounted higher due to limited lateral clearance. Visual evidence: - [Image 3] Figure 2A-2 (panel H, "Overhead sign") illustrates the 17 ft MIN. vertical clearance from the pavement to an overhead-mounted sign, along with the 6 ft MIN. lateral offset to the support. - [Image 5] shows the Section 2A.15 Standard text requiring not less than 17 feet of vertical clearance for overhead signs over the entire width of the pavement and shoulders, plus the Options allowing reduced clearance near lower structures or in tunnels. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Section 2A.16 Standard §1 (p.59) - Section 2G.03 Option §14 (p.411) - Section 2G.08 Option §4 (p.419) - Section 2G.10 Option §18 (p.422) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 100
gold_answer: At least 17 feet, except where nearby structures or special constrained structures qualify for the specific exceptions in Section 2A.15.
